review_note: Field reference. Substance composition and slang change rapidly; treat the patient and toxidrome, not the reported product name.

sources.name: DEA Public Safety Advisory — Emerging Synthetic Drugs

substances.name: Fentanyl / Illicit Opioids
substances.presentation: Decreased LOC, slow or absent respirations, pinpoint pupils, hypoxia/cyanosis; hypotension or bradycardia may occur.
substances.danger: Apnea and recurrent respiratory depression. Counterfeit tablets may contain fentanyl or other synthetic opioids without the patient knowing.
substances.gfd: Airway/ventilation first. Naloxone per GFD protocol when opioid toxicity is suspected. Additional fentanyl, morphine, midazolam, ketamine, or nitrous oxide may worsen CNS/respiratory depression unless clearly indicated for another problem; monitor ventilation closely.
substances.pearl: Clinical response to naloxone supports opioid effect but does not identify the actual street product.

substances.name: Xylazine / Tranq
substances.presentation: Marked sedation, respiratory depression, bradycardia and hypotension; chronic exposure can be associated with significant skin wounds.
substances.danger: Often mixed with fentanyl. Naloxone does not reverse xylazine itself, so persistent sedation may remain after opioid effects improve.
substances.gfd: Support airway and ventilation. If opioid co-exposure is possible, naloxone remains appropriate per GFD protocol. Be cautious with additional sedating medications unless clearly needed for another indication.
substances.pearl: Do not withhold naloxone just because xylazine is suspected; fentanyl co-exposure is common.

substances.name: Medetomidine / “Rhino Tranq”
substances.presentation: Profound sedation, bradycardia, hypotension and respiratory depression; severe withdrawal has been reported with repeated exposure.
substances.danger: Increasingly found with illicit fentanyl. Naloxone will not reverse the non-opioid sedative component.
substances.gfd: Airway/ventilation and hemodynamic support are priorities. Give naloxone per GFD protocol when opioid exposure is suspected. Avoid assuming persistent sedation after naloxone means treatment failure.
substances.pearl: CDC reported substantial U.S. growth in detections through 2025, including the Midwest.

substances.name: Nitazenes
substances.presentation: Opioid toxidrome: CNS depression, respiratory depression/apnea, miosis and hypoxia.
substances.danger: May be present in fentanyl, heroin or counterfeit pills. Some compounds are highly potent and may require repeated naloxone dosing and prolonged reassessment.
substances.gfd: Ventilate first and use naloxone according to GFD protocol; repeat dosing should follow patient respiratory response and protocol. Expect possible recurrence.
substances.pearl: Treat the opioid toxidrome; the exact analog is usually unknown in the field.

substances.name: Cychlorphine
substances.presentation: Expected severe opioid-type CNS and respiratory depression.
substances.danger: DEA has identified it among emerging synthetic drugs being mixed with illicit fentanyl.
substances.gfd: Manage as suspected opioid poisoning: airway/ventilation, oxygenation, naloxone per GFD protocol, and frequent reassessment.
substances.pearl: Field identification is unlikely; consider it part of the evolving synthetic-opioid supply.

substances.name: Benzodiazepines / Counterfeit “Xanax”
substances.presentation: Sedation, slurred speech, ataxia, impaired coordination; severe respiratory depression is more likely with opioids or alcohol.
substances.danger: Counterfeit tablets may contain fentanyl or other substances instead of, or in addition to, a benzodiazepine.
substances.gfd: Support airway/ventilation. If opioid co-exposure is possible, naloxone may improve the opioid component. Additional midazolam, fentanyl, morphine, ketamine or nitrous oxide can increase sedation; use only for a separate clear indication with close monitoring.
substances.pearl: A pill marked like a prescription tablet is not proof of contents.

substances.name: Methamphetamine
substances.presentation: Agitation, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, mydriasis, hyperthermia, chest pain, paranoia or seizures.
substances.danger: Hyperthermia, severe agitation, dysrhythmia, myocardial ischemia and rhabdomyolysis.
substances.gfd: Treat the patient and complication per GFD protocol. Midazolam and/or ketamine may be relevant for severe agitation or seizures when indicated by protocol. Continuous ECG, temperature awareness and supportive care are important.
substances.pearl: Marked agitation plus hyperthermia should raise concern for a time-critical sympathomimetic emergency.

substances.name: Cocaine / Crack
substances.presentation: Tachycardia, hypertension, agitation, diaphoresis, chest pain, mydriasis; seizures or dysrhythmias can occur.
substances.danger: Acute coronary syndrome, malignant dysrhythmias, hyperthermia and seizures.
substances.gfd: Manage chest pain, seizures, dysrhythmia and agitation using the applicable GFD protocol. Aspirin/nitroglycerin or sedation decisions should be driven by the patient’s presentation and protocol, not the street-drug label alone.
substances.pearl: Cocaine-associated chest pain still requires a full ACS evaluation.

substances.name: MDMA / Molly / Ecstasy
substances.presentation: Agitation, tachycardia, diaphoresis, hyperthermia, bruxism, anxiety; altered mental status and seizures may occur.
substances.danger: Hyperthermia, hyponatremia, seizures, serotonin toxicity and dehydration/overhydration complications.
substances.gfd: Supportive care, temperature assessment, ECG monitoring and seizure/agitation management per GFD protocol. Do not assume a product sold as Molly contains only MDMA.
substances.pearl: Severe hyperthermia or neurologic change is a major red flag.

substances.name: Synthetic Cannabinoids / K2 / Spice
substances.presentation: Highly variable: agitation, anxiety, psychosis, vomiting, tachycardia, seizures, sedation or unresponsiveness.
substances.danger: Effects are unpredictable and may be much more severe than cannabis.
substances.gfd: Treat the dominant complication per GFD protocol. Midazolam or ketamine may be relevant for severe agitation/seizures when protocol criteria are met; maintain ECG and airway monitoring.
substances.pearl: A normal-looking cannabis product or vape does not reliably indicate contents.

substances.name: PCP
substances.presentation: Agitation, analgesia, nystagmus, hypertension, altered perception, unusual strength or unresponsiveness.
substances.danger: Violent agitation, hyperthermia, seizures, trauma and rhabdomyolysis.
substances.gfd: Scene safety first. Treat severe agitation/seizure using the appropriate GFD protocol; monitor temperature, ECG, airway and trauma risk.
substances.pearl: Horizontal or vertical nystagmus can support a dissociative toxidrome but is not diagnostic.

substances.name: GHB / GBL
substances.presentation: Rapid-onset sedation, coma, bradycardia, vomiting and respiratory depression; patients may awaken relatively abruptly.
substances.danger: Aspiration and respiratory compromise, especially with alcohol or other depressants.
substances.gfd: Airway protection and ventilation are the priorities. Additional sedatives/opioids can worsen depression and should only be used for a separate indication.
substances.pearl: Abrupt changes in level of consciousness can occur.

substances.name: LSD / Psilocybin / Hallucinogens
substances.presentation: Perceptual changes, anxiety/panic, tachycardia, mydriasis and altered behavior; severe agitation is less common but possible.
substances.danger: Trauma, panic reactions, unsafe behavior, hyperthermia or polysubstance exposure.
substances.gfd: Supportive environment and assessment for co-ingestants/trauma. Treat severe agitation or seizures only when clinically indicated under GFD protocol.
substances.pearl: The major field concern is often behavior, environment, trauma or an unexpected co-ingestant.

substances.name: Ketamine (Illicit/Recreational)
substances.presentation: Dissociation, nystagmus, altered perception, tachycardia/hypertension, sedation or impaired coordination.
substances.danger: Airway risk, aspiration, trauma and polysubstance CNS depression.
substances.gfd: The patient’s illicit exposure is separate from GFD ketamine indications. If GFD ketamine is considered for another reason, account for existing dissociation/sedation and monitor airway/ventilation closely.
substances.pearl: A reported recreational dose does not reliably establish actual concentration or co-ingestants.

substances.name: Kratom / 7-OH
substances.presentation: Can produce stimulant-like effects at lower exposure and opioid-like sedation, nausea, vomiting, respiratory depression or seizures at higher/toxic exposure.
substances.danger: Concentrated 7-OH products are increasingly associated with poisonings; polysubstance use can worsen CNS/respiratory depression.
substances.gfd: Treat the clinical syndrome. Support airway/ventilation; if an opioid-like toxidrome with respiratory depression is present, naloxone may be considered according to GFD opioid-poisoning protocol and patient response.
substances.pearl: DEA St. Louis has specifically highlighted increasing kratom/7-OH poisonings in Missouri.

toxidromes.name: Opioid pattern
toxidromes.findings: Decreased LOC + slow/absent respirations ± pinpoint pupils
toxidromes.action: Ventilate/oxygenate; naloxone per GFD protocol when opioid effect is suspected.
toxidromes.note: Pattern suggests an opioid effect, not a specific product.

toxidromes.name: Sympathomimetic pattern
toxidromes.findings: Agitation + tachycardia + hypertension + diaphoresis + mydriasis ± hyperthermia
toxidromes.action: Supportive care, ECG/temperature monitoring, treat seizures or severe agitation per GFD protocol.
toxidromes.note: Common with methamphetamine, cocaine, MDMA and mixed stimulants.

toxidromes.name: Sedative / depressant pattern
toxidromes.findings: Somnolence, slurred speech, ataxia, bradypnea or hypotension
toxidromes.action: Airway and ventilation first; evaluate for opioid co-exposure and other depressants.
toxidromes.note: Can reflect benzodiazepines, GHB, alcohol, xylazine/medetomidine or mixtures.

toxidromes.name: Dissociative / severe agitation pattern
toxidromes.findings: Agitation, altered perception, nystagmus, analgesia or unusual behavior
toxidromes.action: Scene safety, trauma check, temperature/ECG monitoring, treat severe agitation per GFD protocol.
toxidromes.note: May occur with PCP, ketamine or synthetic cannabinoids.
